General Embryology.question: ১) Which is derivative of 1st pharyngeal arch?
General Embryology.exp:
The 1st pharyngeal (mandibular) arch is associated with the trigeminal nerve (CN V), mainly V3.

Its muscular derivatives include:

  • Muscles of mastication — masseter, temporalis, medial & lateral pterygoids

  • Mylohyoid

  • Anterior belly of digastric

  • Tensor tympani

  • Tensor veli palatini

Why the others are incorrect:

  • Muscles of facial expression → 2nd pharyngeal arch → CN VII

  • Intrinsic muscles of larynx → 6th arch → CN X (recurrent laryngeal)

  • Muscles of tongue → mainly occipital somites → CN XII

Exam pearl:
1st pharyngeal arch → Muscles of mastication → CN V3.

General Embryology.question: ২) What is the site of storage for sperm?
General Embryology.exp:
The epididymis is the main site where sperm are stored and undergo maturation. Sperm acquire motility and fertilizing capacity during their passage through the epididymis.

  • Testis → sperm production (spermatogenesis)

  • Epididymis → sperm maturation and storage

  • Seminal vesicle → produces fructose-rich seminal fluid

  • Vas deferens → transports sperm; can store some sperm temporarily

Exam pearl:
Sperm storage and maturation → Epididymis.

General Embryology.question: ৩) Which is derived from mesoderm?
General Embryology.exp:
The spleen is derived from mesoderm, specifically from mesenchymal cells in the dorsal mesogastrium.

  • Spleen → Mesoderm

  • Parotid gland → Ectoderm

  • Pancreas → Endoderm

  • Thyroid follicular cells → Endoderm (parafollicular C cells are neural crest-derived)

Exam pearl:
Spleen is the classic mesoderm-derived organ among these options.

General Embryology.question: ৪) The process of formation of three germ layers in embryo is called--?
General Embryology.exp:
Gastrulation is the process by which the three primary germ layers are formed in the embryo:

  • Ectoderm

  • Mesoderm

  • Endoderm

Why the others are incorrect:

  • Organogenesis: Formation and development of organs from the germ layers.

  • Embryogenesis: Overall process of embryo development.

  • Cleavage: Rapid mitotic divisions of the zygote following fertilization.

Exam pearl:
Formation of 3 germ layers → Gastrulation.

General Embryology.question: ৫) Which is derivative of midgut?
General Embryology.exp:
The midgut gives rise to:

  • Distal part of duodenum

  • Jejunum

  • Ileum

  • Cecum and appendix

  • Ascending colon

  • Proximal 2/3 of transverse colon

The other options are hindgut derivatives:

  • Descending colon → Hindgut

  • Sigmoid colon → Hindgut

  • Rectum → Hindgut

Exam pearl:
Midgut → Ascending colon + proximal 2/3 of transverse colon.

General Embryology.question: ৬) Melanocytes are derived from which of the following germ layer?
General Embryology.exp:
Melanocytes are derived from neural crest cells, which migrate into the developing skin and differentiate into pigment-producing cells.

  • Neural crest → Melanocytes

  • Surface ectoderm → Epidermis

  • Neural tube → CNS structures

  • Paraxial mesoderm → Somites, vertebrae, skeletal muscle, etc.

Exam pearl:
Melanocyte = Neural crest derivative.

General Embryology.question: ৭) Fetal part of placenta develops from....?
General Embryology.exp:
The fetal part of the placenta develops from the chorion frondosum (villous chorion), which contains the chorionic villi.

The maternal part is derived from the decidua basalis.

  • Fetal part → Chorion frondosum

  • Maternal part → Decidua basalis

Exam pearl:
Placenta = Chorion frondosum (fetal) + Decidua basalis (maternal).

General Embryology.question: ৮) Which period is highly sensitive to teratogen?
General Embryology.exp:
The embryonic period (3rd–8th weeks) is the most sensitive period to teratogens, because this is when organogenesis occurs. Exposure to teratogens during this period can cause major structural congenital abnormalities.

  • Pre-embryonic period (0–2 weeks): “All-or-none” effect—embryo may die or recover without major malformation.

  • Embryonic period (3–8 weeks): Maximum teratogenic sensitivity → major congenital malformations

  • Fetal period (9 weeks to birth): More likely to cause growth restriction and functional/maturation defects.

Exam pearl:
Most sensitive period to teratogens = Embryonic period (3–8 weeks).

General Embryology.question: ৯) Which hormone maintains follicular phase of menstrual cycle?
General Embryology.exp:
The follicular (proliferative) phase of the menstrual cycle is primarily maintained by estrogen, which is produced by developing ovarian follicles under the influence of FSH.

Estrogen causes:

  • Proliferation and thickening of the endometrium

  • Growth of endometrial glands

  • Gradual increase in LH receptor expression and preparation for ovulation

Why the others are less appropriate:

  • Progesterone → Mainly maintains the luteal/secretory phase.

  • FSH → Stimulates follicular development but is not the principal hormone maintaining the endometrial follicular phase.

  • LH → Triggers ovulation and supports the corpus luteum.

Exam pearl:
Follicular/proliferative phase → Estrogen.

General Embryology.question: ১০) What is the normal site of implantation?
General Embryology.option2: posterior wall of uterus near fundus
General Embryology.option3: middle of the fundus of uterus
General Embryology.exp:
The normal site of implantation is the posterior or anterior wall of the upper uterine body, near the fundus, with the posterior wall being classically described as the common site.

  • Ampulla of fallopian tube → Most common site of ectopic pregnancy, not normal implantation.

  • Middle of fundus → Not the classic answer.

  • Round ligament → Not a site of normal implantation.

Exam pearl:
Normal implantation → posterior wall of uterus, near the fundus.

General Embryology.question: ১১) The chorion develops from.....?
General Embryology.exp:
The chorion is the outermost fetal membrane and develops from trophoblast + extraembryonic mesoderm.

For this MCQ, mesoderm is the expected answer because the chorion contains extraembryonic mesoderm.

  • Trophoblast → outer cellular component of chorion

  • Extraembryonic mesoderm → forms the connective tissue core

  • Endoderm → contributes to yolk sac, not chorion

Exam pearl:
Chorion = trophoblast + extraembryonic mesoderm.

General Embryology.question: ১২) Menstrual blood contains which of the following?
General Embryology.exp:
At ovulation, the primary oocyte completes meiosis I and forms a secondary oocyte. The secondary oocyte begins meiosis II but remains arrested at metaphase II.

If fertilization does not occur, the secondary oocyte degenerates and is expelled along with the menstrual blood.

  • Primary oocyte → present before ovulation

  • Secondary oocyte → released at ovulation and may be present in menstrual material

  • Mature ovum → technically formed only after completion of meiosis II, which normally occurs after fertilization

Exam pearl:
Menstrual blood may contain a degenerating secondary oocyte.

General Embryology.question: ১৩) Otic placode gives rise to which of the following?
General Embryology.exp:
The otic placode is an ectodermal thickening that gives rise to the otic vesicle (otocyst), which develops into the membranous labyrinth of the inner ear.

  • Otic placode → Inner ear

  • Lens of eye → Lens placode

  • Oral epithelium → Surface ectoderm/endoderm depending on region

  • Nasal epithelium → Olfactory placode

Exam pearl:
Otic placode → Inner ear.

General Embryology.question: ১৪) What is the basis of axial skeleton?
General Embryology.exp:
The notochord is the embryonic axial skeletal structure and serves as the primary longitudinal axis of the embryo.

It also plays an important role in inducing development of the neural tube and surrounding axial structures. In adults, most of the notochord disappears, with remnants persisting as the nucleus pulposus of intervertebral discs.

Exam pearl:
Basis/primitive axial skeleton → Notochord.

General Embryology.question: ১৫) Palatine tonsil develops from which pharyngeal pouch?
General Embryology.exp:
The palatine tonsil develops from the endoderm of the 2nd pharyngeal pouch.

  • 1st pouch → Auditory (Eustachian) tube and middle ear cavity

  • 2nd pouch → Palatine tonsil

  • 3rd pouch → Inferior parathyroid + thymus

  • 4th pouch → Superior parathyroid

Exam pearl:
2nd pharyngeal pouch → Palatine tonsil.

General Embryology.question: ১৬) Genital tubercle in females gives rise to which of the following?
General Embryology.exp:
The genital tubercle develops into the clitoris in females and the glans penis in males.

  • Genital tubercle → Clitoris

  • Urogenital folds → Labia minora

  • Labioscrotal swellings → Labia majora

  • Vagina → develops mainly from the sinovaginal bulbs (endodermal) and Müllerian derivatives

Exam pearl:
Female genital tubercle → Clitoris.

General Embryology.question: ১৭) Which one is the derivatives of neural crest cell?
General Embryology.exp:
The adrenal medulla is derived from neural crest cells.

  • Adrenal medulla → Neural crest

  • Mammary gland → Surface ectoderm

  • Anterior pituitary → Oral ectoderm (Rathke’s pouch)

  • Parotid gland → Surface ectoderm

Exam pearl:
Neural crest derivative → Adrenal medulla.

General Embryology.question: ১৮) In the process of spermiogenesis there is formation of the following excludes..?
General Embryology.exp:
Spermiogenesis is the process by which spermatids differentiate into mature spermatozoa. Therefore, spermatids are the starting cells, not a structure formed during spermiogenesis.

During spermiogenesis:

  • Acrosome → develops from the Golgi apparatus

  • Nucleus → becomes condensed

  • Tail/flagellum → develops

  • Excess cytoplasm → shed as residual bodies

Exam pearl:
Spermiogenesis = Spermatid → Spermatozoon.
So, spermatids are not formed during spermiogenesis.

General Embryology.question: ১৯) Which one is not a content of umbilical cord?
General Embryology.exp:
The normal umbilical cord contains:

  • Two umbilical arteries

  • One umbilical vein

  • Wharton's jelly

  • Remnants of the allantois

  • Remnant of the vitelline (omphalomesenteric) duct may be present

Therefore, one umbilical artery is not the normal content.

Exam pearl:
Normal umbilical cord = 2 arteries + 1 vein + Wharton's jelly.

General Embryology.question: ২০) What types of cell division occurs during cleavage?
General Embryology.exp:
During cleavage, the zygote undergoes repeated mitotic divisions. These divisions increase the number of cells (blastomeres) without increasing the overall size of the embryo.

  • Mitosis → Cleavage

  • Meiosis → Formation of gametes

  • Amitosis → Not the normal mechanism of cleavage

Exam pearl:
Cleavage = repeated mitotic divisions of the zygote.
